To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) noncooperative entry deterence arises in a market in which firms enter sequentially and irrevocably choose a technology, (2) the earliest firms may choose a normal technology or an inferior technology that partially deters entry, and (3) entry deterence is more likely when the earliest firms choose a normal technology and when the market is characterized by high fixed costs and low demand.

(i) noncooperative entry deterrenec can be implemented by the first firm in a market with a sequential technology choice; (ii) the first firm can implement entry deterrence by delegating this responsibility to subsequent firms; (iii) the first firm may choose to implement only partial entry deterrence; and (iv) the first firm chooses the degree of entry deterrence that maximizes its profit.
